headline: High: shared MCP surfaces and write-capable agentic-flow can drive prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors into OpenBBTerminal workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a exposes MCP and stdin/stdout plus shell-capable tooling, while agent_b also uses MCP and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if agent_a outputs are bridged into agent_b without provenance checks. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a output is forwarded into agent_b MCP or stdin without provenance tagging
IF agent_b treats MCP/stdin content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding between the two agents
Add a provenance prefix to all agent_a outputs before agent_b reads them
Require a human review step before any agent_b tool call
Restrict agent_b parsers to a strict schema
requires-engineering: add channel isolation between MCP sessions

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts, and agent_b touches financial and licensed data. Both expose MCP/stdin surfaces, so shared-workspace or shared-channel leakage is plausible even though neither profile proves a shared filesystem. Because the pairwise bridge is inferred, medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF agent_a can read or emit files containing prompts, code, or repo metadata into a shared channel
IF agent_b receives those artifacts through MCP, REST, or stdin/stdout
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Block sensitive files from being passed through shared MCP tools
Redact prompts and repository metadata before handoff
Audit outbound payloads from agent_a for financial or licensed data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, and modify git state; agent_b cannot write files or modify git, but it does expose MCP and local server surfaces. The main conflict is not direct write-write collision, but agent_a can mutate shared repo state that agent_b may consume. Since no locking or isolation is documented, the interaction is a real default-path risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF agent_b reads artifacts produced after agent_a mutates git or installs packages
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones
Freeze git writes while agent_b is active
Pin package environments before coordination
Use a lockfile or orchestrator mutex
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate and transform content via shell/MCP workflows, and agent_b is a financial-modeling system with MCP/REST interfaces that may consume upstream outputs. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into financial analysis or actions. The lack of documented verification between them pushes this to high.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as input to agent_b without validation
IF agent_b publishes or acts on derived financial results
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require source citations for any factual claim passed from agent_a
Limit agent_b to read-only analysis until reviewed
Log and diff all handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles code, repository metadata, and task prompts, while agent_b handles financial and licensed data. Both are open-source and docs-only, but the profiles show different data classes and no shared retention or residency controls. That creates a compliance mismatch risk, though not enough evidence for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is routed through agent_a's prompt or logging paths
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two agents' storage backends
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable logging of regulated fields in shared pipelines
Document retention settings for both agents
Separate EU or regulated datasets from agent_a workflows
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
